He played high school basketball in [[Fresno, California]], at [[San Joaquin Memorial High School]]. Pondexter played four years of [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]]. At the end of his senior season, he earned first-team [[All-Pac-10 men's basketball team|All-Pac-10]] honors and an All-American honorable mention by the Associated Press.{{cite web|last=Couch|first=Graham|url=https://www.mlive.com/broncos/index.ssf/2010/03/david_kool_is_ap_all-america_h.html |title=David Kool one of state's three AP All-America honorable mentions |work=MLive.com |date=March 29, 2010 |access-date=March 29, 2010}} ==Early life== Pondexter was born on March 10, 1988, in [[Fresno]], [[California]]. As a high school senior, Pondexter was a highly sought after recruit, rated five stars and the 16th best prospect in the 2006 class by Scout.com.{{cite web|title=2006 Top College Basketball Recruits|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&=bb&pid=88&yr=2006|publisher=Scout.com|access-date=November 1, 2013}} Pondexter eventually signed a letter-of-intent with the [[University of Washington]], over scholarship offers from Arizona, Connecticut, and Memphis.{{cite web|title=Quincy Pondexter Player Profile|url=http://washington.scout.com/a.z?s=147&p=8&c=1&nid=1167252|publisher=Scout.com|access-date=November 1, 2013}} Washington's 2006 recruiting class of Pondexter, Spencer Hawes, Adrian Oliver, and Phil Nelson was rated amongst the top in the country. They were ranked sixth overall by Scout.com,{{cite web|title=Class of 2006 Recruiting Rankings|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=14&cfg=bb&yr=2006|publisher=Scout.com|access-date=November 1, 2013}} and eighth overall by Rivals.com.{{cite web|title=Class of 2006 team recruiting rankings|date=November 9, 2005|url=http://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=477059|publisher=Rivals.com|access-date=November 1, 2013|archive-date=November 3, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103210424/http://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=477059|url-status=dead}} As a Senior, He would average 21.5 points, 6.1 rebounds and 1.6 steals. ==College career== ===Freshman season=== As a freshman, Pondexter was selected as a starter in his first collegiate game at Washington, scoring 21 points and grabbing 7 rebounds in a 99–91 win against Pepperdine.{{cite web|title=Young pups lead No. 16 Washington past Pepperdine|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=263160264|publisher=ESPN|access-date=November 1, 2013}} After a hot start, Pondexter endured struggles and fell in the Huskies rotation. However, Pondexter once again began seeing increased playing time near the end of the season, in which the Huskies won 3 of their final 4 games, including wins over #24 USC{{cite web|title=Appleby scores 22, including five 3-pointers, as UW beats USC|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=270600264|publisher=ESPN|access-date=November 1, 2013}} and #2 UCLA.{{cite web|title=Brockman, Hawes lead Huskies to upset of UCLA|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=270620264|publisher=ESPN|access-date=November 1, 2013}} Pondexter finished his freshman season as an honorable mention on the Pac-10 All-Freshman team. His 10.7 ppg was the fourth highest scoring average for a Washington freshman in school history. ===Sophomore season=== At the beginning of his sophomore season, Pondexter regained his spot in the starting lineup. However, seven games into the season he lost his starting position and once again began to slide in the Huskies rotation. Mid-season, fellow sophomore Oliver announced his intention to transfer to [[San Jose State Spartans|San Jose State]]. The departure of Oliver, paired with the loss of Hawes to the [[2007 NBA draft]] and off-season transfer of Nelson to [[Portland State]] left Pondexter as the last remaining member of the previously heralded 2006 recruiting class. Reflecting on his difficult sophomore season and the departure of his classmates, Pondexter said in 2009, "It was really tough my sophomore year. People bond with people in their recruiting class: you come in together, you’re friends. And I was kind of alone sometimes. It was a heart-breaking year for me to see everyone go."{{cite web|last=Ruiz|first=Don|title=Pondexter fills in his story with Adrian Oliver|url=http://blog.thenewstribune.com/uwsports/2009/11/20/pondexter-fills-in-his-story-with-adrian-oliver/|publisher=The News Tribune|access-date=November 1, 2013|archive-date=February 13, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120213000813/http://blog.thenewstribune.com/uwsports/2009/11/20/pondexter-fills-in-his-story-with-adrian-oliver/|url-status=dead}} Pondexter's sophomore struggles extended throughout most of the season, and his scoring average dropped from the previous season to 9.9 ppg. Near the end of the season Pondexter was able to show glimpses of the promise he showed early in his freshman season, averaging 15.2 points and 6.4 rebounds in the final five games of his sophomore season.{{cite web|title=Player Profile: Quincy Pondexter|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/quincy_pondexter_232416.html|publisher=GoHuskies.com|access-date=November 1, 2013|archive-date=July 8, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130708070351/http://www.gohuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/quincy_pondexter_232416.html|url-status=dead}} Following the season, Pondexter won the school's "Industrial Award" as the hardest worker on the team. ===Junior season=== Prior to his junior season, Pondexter was selected as a captain along with senior teammates [[Jon Brockman]] and [[Justin Dentmon]]. The 2008–2009 season got off to a disappointing start, as Washington was upset by Portland in the season opener 80–74.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=283202501 |title=Washington Huskies vs. Portland Pilots - Box Score - November 15, 2008 - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=November 15, 2008 |access-date=November 1, 2013}} In the loss, Pondexter failed to register a point. The source of some initial frustration from Washington fans, Pondexter steadily improved throughout the season as the Huskies climbed to the top of the Pac-10 conference standings. Pondexter lead Washington to a 60-51 road victory over [[USC Trojans|USC]], leading the Huskies with 22 points and 5 rebounds. In a key game against co-leader [[Arizona State Sun Devils|Arizona State]], Pondexter delivered a double-double of 10 points and 12 rebounds in the Huskies 73–70 overtime victory.{{cite web|title=Washington takes 1 1/2 games lead in Pac-10 with OT win|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=290570264|publisher=ESPN|access-date=November 1, 2013}} The victory put Washington in position to claim their first outright Pac-10 conference title since 1953.{{cite web|title=Huskies Claim First Outright Title Since 1953|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290660264|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090312050648/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290660264|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 12, 2009|publisher=ESPN|access-date=November 1, 2013}} One week after the victory against Arizona State, Washington defeated rival [[Washington State Cougars|Washington State]] 67–60 to win the conference title. In the clinching game, Pondexter led the Huskies in scoring with 16 points. Washington finished the season ranked 10th, and earned a 4 seed in the [[2009 NCAA Tournament]]. In Washington's first-round game against Mississippi State, Pondexter lead the team to a 71–58 victory by scoring 23 points and grabbing 7 rebounds.{{cite web|title=Huskies take advantage of Varnado foul trouble in win vs. Bulldogs|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=294000005|publisher=ESPN|access-date=November 1, 2013}} Washington was eliminated in the second round by fifth-seeded Purdue, losing 76–74. In the loss Pondexter delivered a double-double, scoring 20 points and grabbing 10 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=294000006 |title=Purdue Boilermakers vs. Washington Huskies - NCAA Tournament Game - Box Score - March 21, 2009 - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=March 21, 2009 |access-date=November 1, 2013}} ===Senior season=== Prior to his senior season, Pondexter participated in the World University Games, helping the USA claim a bronze medal. Pondexter was once again elected captain of the Huskies. Pondexter was expected to replace the production of Jon Brockman, who had graduated following the 2009 season and was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]]. Pondexter started the season hot, scoring 25 points and grabbing 11 rebounds for the Huskies in a 96–78 victory over [[Belmont University|Belmont]].{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293180264 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091214055259/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293180264 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 14, 2009 |title=Belmont Bruins vs. Washington Huskies - Recap - November 14, 2009 - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=November 14, 2009 |access-date=November 1, 2013}} In the fourth game of the season, the Huskies defeated San Jose State, who were led by former Husky player Adrian Oliver. Following the 80–70 victory in which Pondexter scored 30 points and totaled 15 rebounds, Pondexter said of Oliver, "Adrian, he got what he wanted. He got a school where he can score as many points as he wants. But we’re winning games. He scored 32, I got the win."{{cite web|title=Pondexter fills in his story with Adrian Oliver|url=http://blog.thenewstribune.com/uwsports/2009/11/20/pondexter-fills-in-his-story-with-adrian-oliver/|publisher=The News Tribune|access-date=November 1, 2013|archive-date=February 13, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120213000813/http://blog.thenewstribune.com/uwsports/2009/11/20/pondexter-fills-in-his-story-with-adrian-oliver/|url-status=dead}} Pondexter would have a successful senior season, averaging 19.3 points and 7.4 rebounds. Pondexter won the Pac-10 Conference Player of the Week five times throughout the 2009–2010 season. At the conclusion of the season Pondexter finished second to Cal's [[Jerome Randle]] for Pac-10 Player of the Year, becoming the first Pac-10 player not to win the award despite winning the Player of the Week award five times. However, Pondexter led Washington over Randle's Golden Bears in the 2010 Pac-10 Tournament Championship in a 79–75 victory. Pondexter led the Huskies with 18 points, and clinched an automatic berth for Washington in the [[2010 NCAA Tournament]]. Washington was awarded an #11 seed, and a first round matchup against #6 seed [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]]. In a back-and-forth game, Pondexter banked in the game winning shot with 1.7 seconds remaining to lead the Huskies to an 80–78 upset victory over the Golden Eagles.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300770269 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100320100805/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300770269 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 20, 2010 |title=Washington Huskies vs. Marquette Golden Eagles - NCAA Tournament Game - Recap - March 18, 2010 - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=March 18, 2010 |access-date=November 1, 2013}} The shot capped an 18-point, 11 rebound game for Pondexter, and advanced Washington to a second round matchup against the #3 seeded [[New Mexico Lobos]]. Washington upset New Mexico 82–64, with Pondexter scoring 18 points to lead the Huskies to the Sweet 16 for the first time since 2005–2006.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=300790167 |title=Washington Huskies vs. New Mexico Lobos - NCAA Tournament Game - Box Score - March 20, 2010 - ESPN (2010–2011)=== On June 24, 2010, Pondexter was selected by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] with the 26th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. On July 8, 2010, the [[New Orleans Hornets]] acquired the rights to Pondexter and [[Craig Brackins]] in exchange for the rights to [[Cole Aldrich]] and [[Morris Peterson]].{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Jimmy |title=New Orleans Hornets clear salary, get two rookies in NBA draft |url=https://www.nola.com/hornets/index.ssf/2010/06/new_orleans_hornets_clear_sala.html |website=NOLA.com |access-date=September 4, 2018 |date=June 24, 2010}}{{cite web|url=http://newsok.com/article/3474427|title=Cole Aldrich, Morris Peterson officially join Oklahoma City Thunder|access-date=July 8, 2010}} === Memphis Grizzlies (2011–2017) === On December 24, 2011, one day before the start of the [[2011–12 NBA season]], the Hornets traded Pondexter to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Greivis Vásquez]].{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=8929|title=Hornets trade Quincy Pondexter to Grizzlies for Greivis Vasquez|work=InsideHoops.com|date=December 24, 2011|access-date=October 11, 2013}}{{cite web|last=Reid|first=John|url=http://www.nola.com/hornets/index.ssf/2011/12/new_orleans_hornets_trade_quin.html|title=New Orleans Hornets trade Quincy Pondexter to Memphis Grizzlies for Greivis Vasquez|work=NOLA.com|date=December 24, 2011|access-date=March 30, 2017}} On October 31, 2013, Pondexter signed a four-year, $14 million contract extension with the Grizzlies.{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14707|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Quincy Pondexter to contract extension|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 31, 2013|access-date=November 1, 2013}} After appearing in a 189 games over his first three seasons in the NBA, injury struck him down during the [[2013–14 NBA season|2013–14 season]]. On December 9, 2013, Pondexter was ruled out indefinitely after he was diagnosed with a tarsal navicular [[stress fracture]] in his right foot.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/quincy-pondexter-injury-update-131209|title=Quincy Pondexter injury update|website=www.nba.com|access-date=September 4, 2018}} He subsequently missed the rest of the season after undergoing surgery on December 20.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/pondexter-surgery131220|title=Quincy Pondexter undergoes surgery|website=www.nba.com|access-date=September 4, 2018}} Pondexter returned for the [[2014–15 NBA season|2014–15 season]] and played out the first two months of the season with Memphis. On January 12, 2015, he was traded back to New Orleans, now known as the Pelicans, in a three-team deal that involved the Grizzlies and the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-quincy-pondexter-draft-pick|title=Pelicans Acquire Quincy Pondexter, Draft Pick - New Orleans Pelicans|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 4, 2018}} He enjoyed a career-best tenure with the Pelicans during the second half of the 2014–15 season, averaging 9.0 points per game and registering a career-high 25 points in a 102–96 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]] on February 25, 2015.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20150225/BKNNOP/gameinfo.html|title=Nets at Pelicans|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 4, 2018}} However, injury struck him down again following the Pelicans' 2015 playoff run. On May 6, 2015, Pondexter underwent successful arthroscopic surgery on his left knee.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/quincy-pondexter-undergoes-successful-surgery/|title=Quincy Pondexter Undergoes Successful Surgery|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 4, 2018}} Pondexter was slated to return in November 2015,{{cite web|url=http://www.thebirdwrites.com/2015/10/26/9595252/2015-player-preview-quincy-pondexter|title=2015 Player Preview: Quincy Pondexter|date=October 26, 2015|access-date=September 4, 2018|archive-date=September 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180905024457/https://www.thebirdwrites.com/2015/10/26/9595252/2015-player-preview-quincy-pondexter|url-status=dead}} but after undergoing another round of left knee surgery on January 20, 2016, he was ruled out for the entire 2015–16 season.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--quincy-pondexter-to-have-season-ending-surgery-234256782.html|title=Sources: Quincy Pondexter to have season-ending surgery|access-date=September 4, 2018}} He was expected to make a full recovery for the 2016–17 season,{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/quincy-pondexter-undergoes-successful-surgery-0/|title=Quincy Pondexter Undergoes surgery for a third time on January 4, 2017.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/quincy-pondexter-injury-update-1/4/17/|title=Quincy Pondexter Injury Update 1/4/17 - New Orleans Pelicans|website=[[NBA.com]] }} Following surgery number three, Pondexter battled the life-threatening skin infection [[Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus]].{{cite comeback with Bulls|work=ChicagoTribune.com|date=October 19, 2017|access-date=October 20, 2017}} ===Chicago Bulls (2017–2018)=== On September 1, 2017, Pondexter was traded, along with a 2018 second-round pick and cash considerations, to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Ater Majok]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-quincy-pondexter-future-draft-pick-pelicans|title=Bulls acquire Quincy Pondexter & future draft pick from Pelicans - Chicago Bulls|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 4, 2018}} Despite missing all of preseason with a strained left hamstring, Pondexter played for the first time since April 2015 in the Bulls' 2017–18 season opener on October 19, 2017, against the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974769|title=Valanciunas, Miles help Raptors beat Bulls 117-100 in opener|work=ESPN.com|date=October 19, 2017|access-date=October 19, 2017}} On February 1, 2018, he was waived by the Bulls.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/bulls-waive-quincy-pondexter|title=BULLS WAIVE QUINCY PONDEXTER|work=NBA.com|date=February 1, 2018|access-date=February 1, 2018}} ===San Antonio Spurs (2018–2019)===
